content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], I have [product_name] [version_no] and [article_no]. I understand that for programming on Windows 10, I need [product_name] [version_no] or newer. Will this updated [product_name] be compatible with previous units? Also, can the original connection cable from [company_name] still be used? I'm a beginner and have a straightforward question... [user_name]

If you've installed a full version of [product_name] [version_no], you can upgrade to the latest [product_name] [version_no]. With [product_name] [version_no], you can read and write programs for all [product_name] devices ([article_no] through [product_name] [version_no]). You can also use the same cable for older [product_name] devices.

Dear [user_name], Thank you for your quick reply! My situation is that I have the [version_no] CD, but because I need to move to a new PC with Windows 10, I no longer have [version_no] installed. However, I believe the upgrade works as long as I have the original CD. Thanks again!

You can install the upgrade even if [product_name] is not already installed, as long as you have the original installation CD or DVD. Refer to this FAQ: How do you install a downloaded upgrade for [product_name] with or without previous [product_name] software?

I managed to download [version_no], but not with the export functionality. It's possible to download the demo program, but when I follow the steps and run the setup file, it doesn't prompt for the location of the original CD. Am I missing a step? I've tried several times with the same outcome. Does this mean that I can write programs but need to purchase a new original CD, even though I have the original [version_no] CD? If so, it seems upgrades wouldn't work. But perhaps I'm making a mistake... Has anyone else faced this situation? Thanks, [user_name] [IMAGE]

The demo isn't a full version and therefore doesn't have export restrictions. It also doesn't need an original installation CD, since it's just a demo. Some functions are limited compared to the full version, especially those involving communication with actual [product_name] hardware such as transferring programs to the device or performing online tests.

I understand that the demo version isn't fully featured. What I need is to upgrade [version_no] with export capability. From the instructions, it looks like it should be possible through the upgrade center. However, the only downloadable option seems to be the demo version. Am I searching in the wrong area?

You're checking the wrong location. All the necessary information is in this topic: Download for [product_name] [version_no] Software Upgrade. Your discussion was separated from this main topic. Have you reviewed it?

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are struggling with understanding the steps to upgrade [product_name] software from an older version on a new operating system, using the original CD. There is confusion over the differences between demo and full versions, particularly regarding feature access and upgrade eligibility. The main points of uncertainty are about obtaining the full upgrade and knowing which hardware and software functions remain available post-upgrade.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect seamless backwards compatibility with earlier [product_name] devices, ability to upgrade with the original CD, continued use of original connection cables, and access to all features such as export and direct hardware communication after upgrading.
